result.topic_en: Calculations (June 1856, with an 1857 addition) on the propagation of plane air waves of finite amplitude: the hodograph/Legendre-type transformation that linearises the gas-dynamics equations, the characteristic variables p, q, and the solution of the resulting linear equation by a Riemann-function/series integral.
result.transcription:
Fortpflanzung ebener Wellen in der Luft bei Bewegungen von endlicher Größe. \hfill Juni 1856
$c - a^2\log\varrho = \frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial t} + \frac12\left(\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x}\right)^2 \quad -\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial x}\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x^2}$
$-a^2\frac{\partial s}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial x'}{\partial t} + x'\frac{\partial x'}{\partial x} \quad -\frac{\partial s}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}x' + \frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}$
$dx' = \frac{\partial x'}{\partial t}dt + \frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}dx \quad ds = \frac{\partial s}{\partial t}dt + \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}dx \quad \Delta' = \frac{\partial x'}{\partial t}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}\frac{\partial s}{\partial t} = \left(\frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}\right)^2 - a^2\left(\frac{\partial s}{\partial x}\right)^2$
$\Delta' dt = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}dx' - \frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}ds \quad \Delta' dx = -\frac{\partial s}{\partial t}dx' + \frac{\partial x'}{\partial t}ds$
($\Delta' \gtrless 0$)
$-a^2\frac{\partial t}{\partial x'} = \frac{\partial x}{\partial s} - x'\frac{\partial t}{\partial s}, \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial x'} = \frac{\partial t}{\partial x'}x' - \frac{\partial t}{\partial s}, \quad \frac{\partial(x - x't)}{\partial x'}e^{s} = -\frac{\partial e^{s}t}{\partial s}$
$(x - x't)dx' - a^2 t\,ds = d.$
$\int e^{s}(-t\,dx' + (x - x't)ds) = [-d-] e^{\frac{s}{2}}u$ [?]
$\frac{\partial\left(e^{-s}\frac{\partial(e^{\frac{s}{2}}u)}{\partial x'}\right)}{\partial x'}a^2 = \frac{\partial e^{-s}\frac{\partial e^{\frac{s}{2}}u}{\partial s}}{\partial s} \quad a^2\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x'^2} = \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial s^2} - \frac14 u \quad \frac{x'}{4a} + \frac{s}{4} = p \quad \frac{x'}{4a} - \frac{s}{4} = q, \quad \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial p\partial q} + u = 0$
$e^{\frac{s}{2}}t = -\frac{\partial u}{\partial x'} \quad (x - x't)e^{\frac{s}{2}} = \frac{\partial u}{\partial s} + \frac12 u \quad x e^{\frac{s}{2}} = \frac{\partial u}{\partial s} + \frac12 u - \frac{\partial u}{\partial x'}x'$
$\Delta' = 0. \quad -a^2\frac{\partial s}{\partial x'} - x' = -\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\right) \quad 1 + \frac{\partial s}{\partial x'}\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\right) = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x'}x' + 1 \quad a^2\left(\frac{\partial s}{\partial x'}\right)^2 = 1 \quad s = \pm\frac{x'}{a} + \text{const}\quad \left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\right) = x' \pm a$
$x = t(x' \pm a) + \chi(x')$
[-$\frac{\partial u}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial u}{\partial q} = 0 \quad x = e^{-\frac{p+q}{2}}\left(\frac{\partial u}{\partial p} + u\right)$-]
Dec. 1857.
Jeder bestimmte Werth von p pflanzt sich mit der Geschwindigkeit $\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = \begin{matrix}x'+a\\x'-a\end{matrix}$ fort
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} = -2a(p+q+\frac12)\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} \quad \frac{\partial q}{\partial t} = -2a(p+q-\frac12)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x} \quad \frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial q}{\partial t}\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}2a = \Delta$
$dp = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}(dx - 2a(p+q+\frac12)dt) \quad dq = \frac{\partial q}{\partial x}(dx - 2a(p+q-\frac12)dt)$
$\Delta\frac{\partial t}{\partial q} = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x} \quad \Delta\frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = -\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} \quad \frac{\partial t}{\partial q} = \frac{1}{2a\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}} \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = +\frac{p+q+\frac12}{\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}}$
$\Delta\frac{\partial t}{\partial p} = -\frac{\partial q}{\partial x} \quad \Delta\frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = \frac{\partial q}{\partial t} \quad \frac{\partial t}{\partial p} = -\frac{1}{2a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}} \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = -\frac{p+q-\frac12}{\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = 2a(p+q+\frac12)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q} \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = 2a(p+q-\frac12)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p} \quad \omega = e^{(q-q')+(p-p')}\sum(-1)^n\frac{(p-p')^n(q-q')^n}{\Pi n\,\Pi n} \quad \frac{\partial^2\omega}{\partial p\partial q} - \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p} = 0$
$\frac{\partial^2 t}{\partial p\partial q} + \frac{\partial t}{\partial q} - \frac{\partial t}{\partial p} = 0$
$\int\left(\frac{\partial t}{\partial p} + t\right)\omega\,dp + \left(\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q} + \omega\right)t\,dq \quad \int_{s,q'}^{s,p'} = \int_{q',s}^{q',p'} + \int_{p',q'}^{p',s} \quad \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q} + \omega = 0,\ p = p' \quad \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p} - \omega = 0,\ q = q'$
[Figure: triangle with vertex labels $p=p'$, $q=q'$, $s$]
$t' = t_{q',s}\,\omega_{q',s} + \int_{p',q'}^{s,p'}\left(\frac{\partial t}{\partial p} + t\right)\omega\,dp + \left(\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q} + \omega\right)t\,dq$
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} = 0,\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial t} = 0 \quad [-x-]\ x - 2at(p+q-\frac12) = \varphi(q) \quad \frac{\partial q}{\partial x} = 0\ \frac{\partial q}{\partial t} = 0 \quad [-x-]\ x - 2at(p+q+\frac12) = \varphi(p)$
$dq = \frac{\partial q}{\partial x}(dx - 2a\,dt(p+q-\frac12))$
$4a\,e^{\frac{s}{2}}t = -\frac{\partial u}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial u}{\partial q} \quad 4(x - x't)e^{\frac{s}{2}} = \frac{\partial u}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial u}{\partial q} + 2u \quad w = -u\,e^{p-q} = -u\,e^{\frac{s}{2}} \quad a^2\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x'^2} - \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial s^2} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial s} = 0$
$4(x - x't + at)e^{\frac{s}{2}} = -2\frac{\partial u}{\partial q} + 2u \quad 4(x - x't - at)e^{\frac{s}{2}} = 2\frac{\partial u}{\partial p} + 2u$
$2(x - x't + at)e^{s} = +\frac{\partial w}{\partial q} \quad 2(x - x't - at)e^{s} = -\frac{\partial w}{\partial p} \quad 4at\,e^{s} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} \quad \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q} - \frac{\partial w}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial p}$
$4a\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}e^{s} = \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q} - 2\frac{\partial w}{\partial q} - 2\frac{\partial w}{\partial p}$
$= \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q^2} - 4\frac{\partial w}{\partial p}$

methods.what: Euler equations for 1D isothermal gas flow with velocity potential (Bernoulli and continuity)
methods.quote: $c - a^2\log\varrho = \frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial t} + \frac12\left(\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x}\right)^2 \quad -\frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial\log\varrho}{\partial x}\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x^2}$

methods.what: Equations of motion in terms of velocity x' and s = log density
methods.quote: $-a^2\frac{\partial s}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial x'}{\partial t} + x'\frac{\partial x'}{\partial x} \quad -\frac{\partial s}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}x' + \frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}$

methods.what: Hodograph transformation: interchange dependent and independent variables via Jacobian Δ'
methods.quote: $\Delta' dt = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}dx' - \frac{\partial x'}{\partial x}ds \quad \Delta' dx = -\frac{\partial s}{\partial t}dx' + \frac{\partial x'}{\partial t}ds$

$-a^2\frac{\partial t}{\partial x'} = \frac{\partial x}{\partial s} - x'\frac{\partial t}{\partial s}, \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial x'} = \frac{\partial t}{\partial x'}x' - \frac{\partial t}{\partial s}$

methods.what: Reduction to a telegraph-type equation and its characteristic form in p, q
methods.quote: $a^2\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x'^2} = \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial s^2} - \frac14 u \quad \frac{x'}{4a} + \frac{s}{4} = p \quad \frac{x'}{4a} - \frac{s}{4} = q, \quad \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial p\partial q} + u = 0$

methods.what: Recovery of t and x from potential u
methods.quote: $e^{\frac{s}{2}}t = -\frac{\partial u}{\partial x'} \quad (x - x't)e^{\frac{s}{2}} = \frac{\partial u}{\partial s} + \frac12 u$

methods.what: Degenerate case Δ'=0: simple waves with speed x'±a
methods.quote: $a^2\left(\frac{\partial s}{\partial x'}\right)^2 = 1 \quad s = \pm\frac{x'}{a} + \text{const}\quad \left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\right) = x' \pm a$

methods.what: Riemann invariants p, q transported along characteristics
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} = -2a(p+q+\frac12)\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} \quad \frac{\partial q}{\partial t} = -2a(p+q-\frac12)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$

methods.what: Inverse derivatives of t, x with respect to p, q
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = 2a(p+q+\frac12)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q} \quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = 2a(p+q-\frac12)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}$
$\frac{\partial^2 t}{\partial p\partial q} + \frac{\partial t}{\partial q} - \frac{\partial t}{\partial p} = 0$

methods.what: Riemann function as Bessel-type series solving the adjoint equation
methods.quote: $\omega = e^{(q-q')+(p-p')}\sum(-1)^n\frac{(p-p')^n(q-q')^n}{\Pi n\,\Pi n} \quad \frac{\partial^2\omega}{\partial p\partial q} - \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p} = 0$

methods.what: Characteristic boundary conditions for Riemann function
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial\omega}{\partial q} + \omega = 0,\ p = p' \quad \frac{\partial\omega}{\partial p} - \omega = 0,\ q = q'$

methods.what: Riemann's integration method: solution value as boundary term plus line integral
Simple wave solutions when one invariant is constant
Substitution w = -u e^{s/2} and expressions of x,t via w
methods.quote: $w = -u\,e^{p-q} = -u\,e^{\frac{s}{2}} \quad a^2\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x'^2} - \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial s^2} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial s} = 0$
